candidates.name: Intisar A/103-Brega Gas Pipeline
aka: Zueitina Field 103-Sirte Oil Line 36B Gas Pipeline
Gas Transfer Project 103 Intisar Field to a Coastal Network
candidates.sponsor: National Oil Corporation (NOC), with Sirte Oil Company and Zueitina Oil Company
candidates.from: Intisar A/103 oil field (Zueitina Oil Company concession)
candidates.to: Brega coastal gas distribution network, tying into Sirte Oil's 42-inch Line 36B at the Km 91 complex

evidence.note: NOC Chairman Masoud Suleiman marks completion/commissioning of a 42-inch, 130km gas pipeline from Zueitina Oil Company's Field 103 to Sirte Oil Company's Line 36B, tying in at the Km 91 complex; ~150 MMcf/d capacity; construction had been halted since before 2011 and only now finished by Libyan technical teams from Sirte Oil and Zueitina Oil.

NOC launches trial operation of the 42-inch, ~130km pipeline linking the Intisar A/103 field to the Brega gas distribution network; recovers ~150 MMcf/d of gas previously flared from Intisar, Irada and Sahel fields; project stalled 16+ years before this 2026 trial run.

Confirms the 130km/42-inch pipeline trial (Intisar A/103 to Brega), eliminating back-pressure that had disrupted eastern-field production, part of NOC's push toward 1 Bcf/d and expanded Greenstream exports.

candidates.why_maybe_new: A named 42-inch, 130km transmission line running Intisar A/103 field (via Zueitina Oil Co. Field 103) to the Brega network/Sirte Line 36B at Km 91, completed/commissioned April 2026 after a 16-year construction halt. No roster entry matches this route or these specs under any of its names (Intisar A/103, Zueitina Field 103, Line 36B). Closest existing rows are P1856 Intesar-Brega Gas Pipeline (same 42in diameter, but len=333km, already status=operating, and no field-103/Km-91 tie-in mentioned) and P1872 Km-91.5-Brega Gas Pipeline (len=184, dia=36/16, already operating) - this may be a parallel/second line into the same corridor rather than a wholly distinct new corridor, so the consolidator should judge whether it merges into P1856 (as a '/Pipeline 2') or stands alone given the differing length/diameter-detail and the explicit 16-year-stalled construction history.

candidates.name: Farigh-Brega Gas Pipeline
candidates.sponsor: National Oil Corporation (NOC); Farigh field operated by Waha Oil Company (NOC/TotalEnergies/ConocoPhillips JV)
candidates.from: Farigh gas field (Zueitina axis, Field 103A), Sirte Basin
candidates.to: Brega coastal gas network, connecting to the 42-inch trunkline at Km 91

evidence.note: NOC inaugurates first phase of the Farigh-Brega gas pipeline: a 30km segment from the Farigh field (Zueitina axis/Field 103A) tying into the existing 42-inch trunkline at Km 91, feeding the Brega coastal hub and national grid; gas pumping and pressure balancing underway for end-of-month integration.

Confirms the 30km initial phase of the Farigh-Brega pipeline is operational with gas flow initiated; full-capacity target of 2 Bcf/d referenced for 2030, implying further phases/expansion still to come.

Reiterates the Farigh field-to-Brega routing via the Zueitina-axis Field 103A tie-in to the Km-91 42-inch pipeline, and NOC as sponsor; describes it as strengthening supply to Brega refineries/petrochemical and power-generation plants.

candidates.why_maybe_new: A newly named, explicitly phased (phase 1 of a multi-phase build) transmission line from the Farigh field to Brega via a Km-91 tie-in point; no roster row carries this Farigh-Brega name or route. Farigh field otherwise only appears on the roster via P1861 Farigh-Intesar Gas Pipeline (Farigh field->Intesar Oil field, dia 24, operating) and P3988 Fargh-Sarir Gas Pipeline (Farigh->Sarir) - both different destinations (Intesar/Sarir, not Brega), so this looks like a distinct new corridor out of the same field rather than a duplicate of either. Only the 30km first phase is confirmed built/flowing; marked 'construction' rather than 'operating' given the explicit multi-phase build-out still underway toward a stated 2030 full-capacity target.
